This case will be taken up at 4 PM as this Court is not satisfied with the medical certificate produced by the counsel for the State Shri Manas Mani Verma seeking condonation of presence of the Collector, Rewa on the ground of some illness of her husband.
I have carefully perused the prescription.

It only advises bed rest for 5 days, warm fomentation, no massage and prescribes the following medicines:-
- Tab Ibu+para - Tab Pantop 40 - Tab Nemocid NT This prescription does not disclose any serious medical condition to call for condoning the presence of the Collector, Rewa, therefore, she is directed to remain present at 4 PM before this Court, failing which this Court may draw appropriate proceedings against her.
Matter will be taken up at 4 PM.

sentences.text: Three arguments have been put-forth by Shri H.S. Ruprah, learned Addl.
Advocate General for the State, namely:
"(i) Petitioner had refused to accept the compensation and therefore, petition deserves to be dismissed.

(ii) Petitioners had filed a Misc. Petition before the High Court seeking enhancement of compensation and that Misc. Petition was registered as M.P. No. 2559 of 1993,
therefore, compensation was not paid.
(iii) Since, there was an stay from the High Court, therefore, compensation could not be paid."
When examined, then in support of first argument, contradictory statements are being made in the open Court by learned Addl. Advocate General and the Collector, Rewa.
They have changed the track and say that, petitioner never approached the Collector to seek compensation.

When learned Collector, Rewa is requested to show legal provision forcing a land oustee to approach the Collector and beg for compensation, she is not in a position to assist the Court, though she submits that she has read the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

Perusal of order dated 03.09.1993 passed in M.P. No. 2559 of 1993, 3 WP-11203-2015 reveals that the stay was only in relation to dispossession and there is no mention of the fact of not paying the compensation for the land already acquired.

There is a reference to the order dated 19.08.1993 passed in M.P. No. 2559 of 1993 which reads as under:
"Petitioner No.6 present in person.
He is heard on I.A. No. 6848/93 for further orders on stay.
The notices as directed by this Court's order dated 30.06.1993 have not been issued even though the P.F. was paid in time.
Apparently this is a mistake of the office of the High Court.

Considering the fact that the petitioners are likely to dispossessed, it is directed that the possession of the petitioners over the land under acquisition will not be disturbed until further orders of this Court.
Notices as per the order of this Court, dated 30.06.1993 be issued immediately and the matter be listed as soon the respondents are served."
Thus, it is evident that the award was never stayed by Hon'ble Division Bench of this High Court.
In fact, this Misc. Petition came to be dismissed vide order dated 25.06.2002.
Copy of the order is produced by Shri Ruprah alongwith Chronological Events/Synopsis which is undated and it has been handed over to the Court today during the open Court proceedings.

Thus, now the onus is on the Collector to explain, that once this petition was dismissed in the year,
2002 firstly when notices were issued to the petitioners asking them to collect compensation or Rajesh Kumar Tiwari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167205547/
2 sending the cheque of compensation.

If any 4 WP-11203-2015 cheque/draft was prepared in the name of the petitioner, photo-copy of the same will also be enclosed by the Collector.
She will also point out that what legal opinion was taken in regard to the orders of the High Court dated 19.08.1993 and 03.09.1993.
She will also point out from the order-sheets of the file that taking these orders into consideration, Collector or the Land Acquisition Officer had directed to not to disburse the compensation.
Collector will also point out that when the petition was dismissed vide order dated 25.06.2002, then what stapes were taken to disburse compensation in favour of the petitioner.
Let, these documents be filed by tomorrow i.e. on 08.01.2025.
This case will be taken up at 02:30 p.m. on 08.01.2025.
Collector, Rewa is directed to remain personally present before this Court on 08.01.2025 at 02:30 p.m.
